source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Dejounte Murray
injuries.short_comment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injuries.long_comment: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

injuries.name: Trendon Watford
injuries.short_comment: Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Oklahoma City.
injuries.long_comment: Watford will miss a seventh consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a definitive return timetable.

injuries.name: Bryce McGowens
injuries.short_comment: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
injuries.long_comment: McGowens will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. He's without a timetable to return and can be considered week-to-week until the Pelicans offer an update on his status.

injuries.name: Bennedict Mathurin
injuries.short_comment: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
injuries.long_comment: Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

injuries.name: Dylan Harper
injuries.short_comment: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

injuries.name: Jayden Quaintance
injuries.short_comment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injuries.name: Tobias Harris
injuries.short_comment: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
injuries.long_comment: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

injuries.name: Trey Murphy III
injuries.short_comment: Murphy (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
injuries.long_comment: Murphy missed six consecutive games due to bilateral patellar tendinopathy before returning for Friday's game against the Thunder, when he played 29 minutes and finished with 17 points, four rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block in a 126-120 loss for the Pelicans. He'll sit for the second leg of a back-to-back set, which means more minutes will be available for Jordan Poole, Herbert Jones and Derik Queen. Murphy's next opportunity to play is Monday against the Suns.
